variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: A split in {party} has produced the new party {splinter}.
variants.body:
The party {party} has split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

Workers deserve political organisations that take their interests seriously, whether those organisations stand together or apart. A split should be judged with that purpose in mind. Labour gains little from celebrating an internal victory if the question of a decent working life disappears behind the competing party labels.

The responsibility of {target} should be considered without presuming the split's cause or its eventual consequences. This account records an organisational division and reserves judgment on particulars not supplied. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
